title: What If the Whole World Stayed Home?

scenes.text: What if the whole world stayed home? In April 2020 it nearly did, and scientists measured it.
Daily carbon dioxide emissions fell about seventeen percent, from roughly one hundred million tons to about eighty-three million.
Emissions from cars and trucks dropped about thirty-six percent. Road transport made up forty-three percent of the total drop.
Flights fell hardest, but aviation is only about three percent of global emissions, so it was around ten percent of the drop.
Over the full year, emissions were projected to fall between four and seven percent.
The world paused almost everything, and on the worst day emissions still fell by less than a fifth.
